---
title: "Data"
---

Source files and analysis outputs, about 185 GB, are kept outside the repository. The
code finds them through one setting, `DATA_ROOT`.

## Data root

The code takes `DATA_ROOT` from the first of these that is set:

1. environment variable `MS_FORESTS_VPD_DATA`
2. `DATA_ROOT` in `config/settings.local.yaml`, not under version control
3. `DATA_ROOT` in `config/settings.yaml`, the committed default

```bash
# Windows PowerShell
$env:MS_FORESTS_VPD_DATA = "D:/ms-forests-vpd-data"

# macOS / Linux
export MS_FORESTS_VPD_DATA=/data/ms-forests-vpd-data
```

Or in `config/settings.local.yaml`:

```yaml
DATA_ROOT: D:/ms-forests-vpd-data
```

All other paths in `config/settings.yaml` are relative to `DATA_ROOT`. `src/paths.py`
resolves them and raises an error on import if the folder is missing.

## Folder layout

```
<DATA_ROOT>/
└── data/
    ├── 00_raw/
    │   ├── ameriflux/
    │   ├── fluxnet_from_carbonportal/
    │   ├── fluxnet_from_fluxnetorg/
    │   ├── from-fluxnet-shuttle/
    │   └── japanflux/
    └── outputs/
        ├── 10_datasets/
        ├── 20_subsets/
        ├── 30_shap/
        ├── 40_aggregation/
        ├── 50_plots/
        └── 80_info/
```

Each `00_raw/<source>/` folder holds the unpacked site archives and a `0-info/` folder
with the site metadata file. `config/settings.yaml` gives the file name patterns per
source.

## Source datasets

The analysis uses half-hourly FLUXNET-formatted files from five sources. If a site
appears in more than one, the higher-priority source wins and the others extend the
record backwards (`src/files.py::create_parquet_files`).

| Source | Access |
|--------|--------|
| FLUXNET-SHUTTLE | <https://fluxnet.org/> |
| FLUXNET2015 (ICOS Carbon Portal) | <https://www.icos-cp.eu/> |
| FLUXNET2015 (fluxnet.org) | <https://fluxnet.org/data/fluxnet2015-dataset/> |
| AmeriFlux FLUXNET | <https://ameriflux.lbl.gov/> |
| JapanFlux2024 | <https://www.japanflux.org/> |

All five require registration, so the raw files are not redistributed here.

## Deposited outputs

The analysis outputs are deposited in the ETH Research Collection:
<https://doi.org/10.3929/ethz-c-000798579>. The deposit holds:

- one zip archive per output stage (`10_datasets`, `20_subsets`, `30_shap`,
  `40_aggregation`, `50_plots`, `80_info`), with paths relative to `outputs/`
- `ms-forests-vpd_SourceData.zip`, the data behind every figure, table and
  Supplementary Data file, one or more files per display item
- `ms-forests-vpd_demo.zip`, the model input of one site for the demo
  ([Installation](installation.qmd#demo))
- `ms-forests-vpd_code.zip`, a snapshot of this repository in the version used for the
  paper
- `DATA_FLOW.html`, the data flow chart with the archive of each file
- `MANIFEST.csv`, a SHA-256 checksum for every deposited file

The [data flow chart](data_flow.html) shows which archive holds each file.

## Entry points

- With the stage archives unpacked into `outputs/`, every stage from `30_shap` onward and
  every figure runs without the raw source files. These stages start from
  `outputs/20_subsets/`, one small parquet file per site. Rebuild those from raw data only
  if the site selection or the filtering changes.
- With `30_shap/` unpacked as well, the aggregation and the figures run without refitting
  the models. The figure scripts read `outputs/40_aggregation/`, `outputs/30_shap/` and
  `outputs/80_info/`.

## ERA5 credentials

Only scripts `16a` to `16d`, which rebuild the climate normals, need these credentials.

- Google Earth Engine (`16a`, `16b`): an Earth Engine account and cloud project.
  Authenticate once with `earthengine authenticate`.
- Copernicus Climate Data Store (`16c`, `16d`): a CDS account and an API key in
  `~/.cdsapirc`. Requests are queued server-side and can take hours.

Script `17` merges whatever is present (see [Methods](methods.qmd#era5-climate-normals)).
